rulings.dimensionIndependence: Authentication identity, Principal, Employee link, Job Role, Security Role, Work Eligibility, Operational Scope, Operating Company, Warehouse, ownership, accountability and assignment are TWELVE separate facts. No dimension in this manifest is derived from another, and the validator refuses any entry that would derive one.
rulings.eligibilityGrantsNothing: A Work Eligibility code confers no Security Role, no capability, no permission, no Job Role, no ownership, no assignment and no operating-company authority. It is only ever a SECONDARY business restriction on top of a capability that was checked first.
rulings.scopeIsNotAssignment: OPERATIONAL_SCOPE answers 'where may this Employee work'. RECORD_ASSIGNMENT answers 'is this record theirs'. They are unrelated facts and neither implies the other.
rulings.noLegacyLabels: No legacy operationalRoles value (PARTS_ASSOCIATE, WAREHOUSE_ASSOCIATE, TECHNICIAN, PARTS_MANAGER, WAREHOUSE_MANAGER) appears as a qualification code. The governed vocabulary names a KIND OF WORK, never a role bundle. The validator refuses the legacy strings by name.
rulings.capabilityFirst: Every expectation in contextualExpectations is evaluated capability-first. A persona lacking the capability is expected to be refused CAPABILITY_MISSING and nothing about the record is expected to be revealed.
rulings.noAuthenticationInvented: This manifest invents no authentication. Interactive login for every persona named here is the Sample Company v2 Firebase sandbox path, unchanged. A fixture Principal under `eos-synthetic-nonprod` still cannot sign in.

owner-executive.separationReason: OWNER RULING. The merged persona held `admin` and claimed the Administrator authority was the same authority. It is not, and the database says so: `owner` holds 47 granted capabilities, `admin` holds 66, `owner` is a STRICT SUBSET and 19 capabilities -- every operational execution act in Inventory, Equipment, Work Order lifecycle and agreement acceptance -- are admin-only (measured nonprod 2026-09-24). The separation is NOT made by copying Administrator permissions onto the Owner: the `owner` Role is withheld from this seed's grant reconciliation for exactly that reason, and the Owner / Executive persona takes the `owner`-holding Principal that ALREADY EXISTS in nonprod and had no Employee link at all.
owner-executive.$comment: The Owner / Executive is the broadest BUSINESS authority and deliberately holds no Work Eligibility and no Operational Scope: the person who owns the company is not thereby qualified to perform warehouse work or entitled to a queue.

administrator.separationReason: OWNER RULING: Administrator is not Owner and Owner is not Administrator, and no merged Owner/Admin fixture may survive as the canonical acceptance persona. The previous catalog recorded this as MERGED_INTO_OWNER_EXECUTIVE on the argument that a second Principal holding `admin` would answer identically on every operation -- which was true of a second ADMIN Principal and was never the question. The two personas differ because they hold DIFFERENT ROLES: `admin` and `owner` are two Roles with two different live grant sets, and the merged fixture hid that by giving the Owner the Administrator's Role.
administrator.$comment: This persona holds the ONE reused real sandbox administrator Principal -- never recreated, never re-credentialed, its Role set never changed. Sample Company v1 linked that Principal to the Owner / Executive Employee; v2 links it here, which is the whole content of the separation on the identity side.

The Job Role used to be spelled FINANCE_MANAGER and the argument used to rest on the shared word; the 2026-09-25 canonical ruling retired that spelling BECAUSE `financeManager` is a Security Role key, so what is left is the stronger form of the same point: the position covers the whole finance function and names no Role at all. It holds no Work Eligibility and no Operational Scope: recording an adjustment is a capability, not a kind of field work, and it happens nowhere in particular.

The Employee record is added so the canonical population is complete and the gap is counted; no Principal and no Security Role is given, because reportViewer / reportFinanceViewer / reportAuthor declare 27 / 5 / 3 capabilities in the compiled catalog and ZERO of them are registered in eos_policy.capabilities -- so a grant here would grant nothing resolvable and would make a domain cutover look finished. No report permission may be granted while the capability is outside or inactive relative to eos_policy.

It shares the OFFICE_MANAGER Job Role with office-manager, whose Security Role is `officeManager`, which is the mirror image of the retail-vs-national-accounts proof: same Job Role, different Security Role.

RUNNABLE TODAY. The open eos_ops.work_order_assignments row names this work order and synthetic-np-emp-service-technician-a. Previously this expectation named reorder request RR-2026-000901 and declared `requires: REORDER_ASSIGNMENT_NOT_SEEDED` -- a blocker that was real for the Reorder path and had nothing to do with this proof.

Technician B is identical to A in Security Role, Job Role and Work Eligibility. The ONLY difference is the assignment row, which is the point -- and it is now a difference that exists in the database rather than one waiting on a seed.

Two independent paths to the same answer, both live for this persona: the open assignment row, and the CURRENT SERVICE_TECHNICIAN Work Eligibility. The earlier second path named a REORDER_QUEUE:sample-co-synthetic scope that this persona has never held and that the operational_scope_target_exists trigger refuses anyway -- an alternative path that could never be taken is not an alternative path.
The same capability reaches the shared queue with NO assignment. Proves neither path implies the other.

The purchasingManager Role carries reorder.purchaseOrder.create unconditionally (migration 1761696000000 grant block). Adding the WORK_ELIGIBILITY predicate to the ACTION narrows it without touching the grant.

THE WITHHELD CRED CELL, ASSERTED. Migration 1761696000000 deliberately excluded `technician` from both purchaseOrder.read (11 Roles granted, technician withheld) and purchaseOrder.create (5 Roles granted, technician withheld), because the legacy grants were conditioned on operationalRoleActive(PARTS_ASSOCIATE) and granting the plain capability would drop the gate. THIS MANIFEST IS THE FIRST THING THAT MAKES THAT SENTENCE FALSE.

contextualExpectations.why: ONE PERSONA, BOTH ANSWERS. No second login: the record setup (which warehouse the action names) carries the whole difference.

The dispatcher has the capability AND the queue scope AND is refused, on the qualification alone. Order matters: eligibility is checked before scope, so the refusal never reveals whether the scope would have passed.

A policy naming the LEGACY operationalRoles value must fail closed with a DISTINCT reason -- 'this platform cannot decide whether you are eligible', not 'you are not eligible'. This expectation is what stops the legacy label creeping back in as a qualification code.
contextualExpectations.$comment: declaredOnly: this predicate is never written to any table. It is an ACTION-side assertion evaluated against GOVERNED_QUALIFICATION_CODES, which is why a persona holding PARTS_OPERATIONS still fails it.

contextualExpectations.why: HONEST GAP. RecordContext accepts exactly two recordKinds -- reorderRequest and workOrder -- and ASSIGNMENT_RELATIONS has no opportunity entry. There is no RECORD_OWNERSHIP predicate kind at all: CONTEXT_PREDICATE_KINDS is exactly WORK_ELIGIBILITY, OPERATIONAL_SCOPE, RECORD_ASSIGNMENT. provisioningContract.safeReset: endEmployeeWorkEligibility / endEmployeeOperationalScope close the open interval and NEVER delete. History keeps both periods. A reset is an END followed by an ASSIGN, which appends rather than rewrites.

jobRoleAuthority.$contract: THE THIRD GOVERNED WORKFORCE AUTHORITY THIS MANIFEST SEEDS. Work Eligibility answers 'qualified for what kind of work', Operational Scope answers 'where', and JOB ROLE answers 'what is this person's BUSINESS FUNCTION' -- and it answers nothing else. A Job Role grants no permission, implies no Work Eligibility, implies no Operational Scope and is never inferred from a Security Role.
